Research prototype · tested on 28 people the model never saw

EEG Arousal Monitor

From EEG alone, once per fMRI volume, it estimates the brain-wide BOLD fluctuation that arousal drives and flags the least vigilant stretches of a scan. The traces below are real ds006040 resting runs (another site, another scanner) scored against their measured fMRI.

Eyes open is the harder case: the model was trained on eyes-closed rest.

EEG vigilance (robust z) Global BOLD predicted from EEG Global BOLD measured by fMRI Flagged low vigilance

How well it tracks

Mean over people; 95% intervals over people. Streaming uses only EEG recorded so far, as it would during a scan.

Does it work as QC?

Spearman ρ across runs. A useful QC score should track the global-signal swing actually measured by fMRI.

How it works

  1. Take the 24 s of EEG before each fMRI volume from 26 standard channels and measure log power in 1 Hz bins (1–45 Hz) over twelve 2 s slices.
  2. Apply a ridge-regression model trained on 22 people from another site (VU). Features are standardised within the recording, so no fMRI is needed.
  3. Report the predicted brain-wide BOLD and an alpha / (delta + theta) vigilance index averaged over the last 8 s; flag stretches where vigilance stays more than 1 robust SD below the run's median for at least 10 s.

What is validated: the predicted global BOLD (against fMRI, above) and the run-level arousal fluctuation as a QC score. What is not yet: the low-vigilance flags, which need eye tracking or sleep scoring to check.

Research tool, not a medical device. Accuracy depends on how much arousal varies in a run, and the vigilance flag is relative to the run itself, not an absolute sleep stage. Code: app/arousal_monitor in the NeuroBOLT repository.
